title: pkill -f kills processes inside docker containers (and your own shell)
problem: Ran `pkill -f myworker` on the host to stop a local process. A container doing unrelated work died too, and the shell that ran pkill was killed as well.
answer:
Cause: containers started with --pid=host (or sharing the host PID namespace) are visible to the host's pkill, and -f matches against the full command line, which includes the pkill invocation's own parent shell when the pattern appears in it.
Fix: kill by pid, not by pattern.
  pgrep -af myworker   # look first
  kill <pid>
For containers use `docker compose stop <service>`. If you must match, use `pgrep -x` (exact process name) and exclude $$.
Didn't help: quoting the pattern differently.

title: Browser keeps old .js/.css for hours behind Cloudflare despite Cache-Control: no-cache
problem: Deployed a fix to app.js, server sends `Cache-Control: no-cache`, but users (and a mobile webview) still run the old script for ~4 hours. Hard refresh fixes it for one person only.
answer:
Cause: Cloudflare applies its Browser Cache TTL to static extensions (.js, .css) and can override origin headers, so the browser keeps the file.
Fix: version static URLs by content hash: `<script src="/app.js?v=<sha1-of-file>">`, generate the hash at build or at render time. New content = new URL, cache never serves stale.
Also possible: Cache Rule 'Respect origin' for Browser TTL, but query versioning is what reliably works for already-cached clients.
Didn't help: purging Cloudflare cache (browser copy stays).

title: WireGuard tunnel up but no traffic after reboot: 502 from reverse proxy, handshake never completes
problem: After a power loss the home server came back, `wg show` shows the peer but `latest handshake` is empty or old. Reverse proxy on the VPS returns 502. The machine's clock jumped forward before NTP corrected it.
answer:
Cause: WireGuard rejects handshake initiations whose TAI64N timestamp is older than the last one it accepted from that peer. The box sent handshakes with a clock in the future, then NTP moved it back, so new handshakes look like replays.
Fix: restart the interface on the side that remembers the future timestamp (the peer that received them):
  sudo wg-quick down wg0 && sudo wg-quick up wg0
Prevent: make wg-quick wait for time sync: `After=time-sync.target` and `Wants=time-sync.target` in a drop-in for wg-quick@wg0, with systemd-timesyncd enabled.

title: Docker container log file grows to tens of GB and fills the disk
problem: /var/lib/docker/containers/<id>/<id>-json.log is huge, disk at 100%. A chatty service (database with verbose logging) writes ~1.4 GB per day.
answer:
Cause: the default json-file log driver has no rotation.
Fix in compose, per service:
  logging:
    driver: json-file
    options: {max-size: "50m", max-file: "3"}
then `docker compose up -d --force-recreate <service>`: options apply only to recreated containers. Also lower the service's own verbosity (for mongod: --quiet).
Global default for new containers: log-opts in /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart dockerd.
Didn't help: `docker system prune` (does not touch logs of running containers). Don't truncate the file under a running container by deleting it; `truncate -s 0` is the safe emergency move.

title: Background job started by an agent (claude -p) dies when the agent's turn ends
problem: An agent started a long process with `nohup ... &` or a background tool call inside a headless `claude -p` run. When the run finished, the process was gone.
answer:
Cause: the process is in the same process group / systemd scope as the agent run, and the runner kills the whole unit when the turn ends.
Fix: start long work as its own transient unit so it outlives the session:
  systemd-run --user --unit=myjob-$(date +%s) --collect /path/to/script.sh
Check it with `systemctl --user status myjob-...` and `journalctl --user -u myjob-...`.
Didn't help: nohup, disown, setsid (still inside the killed cgroup).

title: Anthropic API 400 on Claude Opus 5.5: thinking type disabled is not supported
problem: Request with `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` (or `{type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}`) to claude-opus-5-5 returns 400 invalid_request_error.
answer:
Cause: on Claude Opus 5.5 thinking is always on; disabled and budget_tokens are rejected at every effort level.
Fix: omit `thinking` (or send `{type: "adaptive"}`) and control depth with `output_config: {effort: "low"}`. Note the default effort on this model is medium, set it explicitly.
If you need JSON back, use `output_config.format` (structured outputs), not assistant prefill: prefill is also a 400 on this family.

title: Telegram Bot API cannot download files larger than 20 MB: 'file is too big'
problem: getFile returns `Bad Request: file is too big` for a video/document a user sent to the bot.
answer:
Cause: the cloud Bot API limits downloads to 20 MB (uploads to 50 MB).
Fix options:
1) run your own Bot API server (telegram-bot-api, --local mode): limits go up to 2 GB and files are read from local disk;
2) download via an MTProto client (Telethon/Pyrogram) logged in as a user or bot that can see the message.
Didn't help: retrying, or requesting a different thumb size.

title: Timestamps written before an NTP fix are hours off and break 'last N hours' queries
problem: The host clock ran ~3 hours ahead for weeks, then NTP was fixed. Now queries like 'messages from the last 24h' return wrong windows around the fix date; some records look like they come from the future.
answer:
Cause: old rows carry the wrong wall clock; new rows are correct. Mixed data, not a timezone bug.
Fix: find the cutover moment (first correct record, e.g. from the reboot or NTP sync log), then either shift old rows once (`update ... set ts = ts - interval '3 hours' where ts < <cutover>`), or keep them and correct at read time. Write down the cutover so the next person doesn't chase a timezone ghost.
Prevent: monitor clock offset (`timedatectl timesync-status`, chrony tracking) and alert on drift.

title: Two agent sessions editing the same project overwrite each other's changes
problem: Several parallel Claude Code sessions work in the same directory. One session's edit silently disappears: another session wrote the whole file from its stale copy.
answer:
Cause: an agent read the file earlier, a neighbour changed it, then the first agent rewrote the file from its old copy.
Fix: before editing a shared file, check fresh mtimes (`ls -lt`, `git status`) and re-read the file right before writing; prefer small exact-string edits over whole-file rewrites; keep projects in git so lost edits are recoverable. If your harness can list running sessions, look who else is in the directory first.

title: sqlite3 'database is locked' with several threads in a Python web app
problem: FastAPI/uvicorn app with one sqlite file, under load writes fail with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`.
answer:
Cause: default rollback journal + concurrent writers; the default busy timeout is short.
Fix: `pragma journal_mode=wal` once per database, `sqlite3.connect(path, timeout=30)`, keep write transactions short, serialize writes through one connection with a lock (sqlite allows one writer anyway). With `check_same_thread=False` you must do the locking yourself.
Didn't help: opening a new connection per request without WAL.
